title: The Unofficial Recipe
premise: Tamsin Marchetti, seventeen, has kept his family afloat and himself invisible for two years while his mother works hospital night shifts. When the ghost haunting Hollow Creek High begins leaving him handwritten notes in ink that vanishes by morning — notes that know things no one should know — Tamsin is dragged into a mystery tied to the school's founding and to his own late father's erased history. As he chases the ghost's identity through archives, recipes, and rumors, he must also lead his ragtag culinary club to the state championship his principal wants buried. The ghost turns out to be the memory of Marisol Vane, a student expelled in 1979 for teaching immigrant families to read through cooking classes, whose story was scrubbed from school records; helping her be remembered forces Tamsin to stop hiding, win both championships, and finally let his family see how much he's been carrying.
about_author: Orsen Yarrow is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six years writing stories on the backs of order tickets during slow shifts. They live near a defunct high school rumored to be haunted, which they neither confirm nor deny.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Full-Time Job
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A chaotic morning: burnt toast, missing bus fare, little sister Nia's forgotten field trip form, all managed invisibly before first period. Establishes his rule: don't get noticed, don't need anything. Emotional beat: weary competence masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Note in Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He finds a note in his locker addressed 'Tamsin Marchetti' — in shimmering ink that fades to blank within minutes. No one saw anyone near his locker. His best friend Dev jokes about the ghost; Tamsin feels seen for the first time in years and hates how much he likes it. Beat: unease mixed with longing.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, flashback woven in. We learn how Dad died, how Mom took nights at St. Ambrose, how Tamsin became the household engine. He recites his three rules to himself as he cooks dinner for four. Beat: tenderness under pressure; the cost of being fine.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Principal Hargrove strong-arms the nearly-dead culinary club into entering the regional cook-off purely for PR, then slashes its budget. Tamsin, reluctantly club president, inherits a team of misfits and a trophy case full of gaps. Beat: cynical humor hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Second Note: She Knows My Middle Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Another note appears inside his chemistry textbook, referencing something only his father ever called him. He stakes out his locker after school and catches nothing but cold air and the smell of cardamom. Beat: fear tipping toward obsession.

chapters.title: The Misfit Brigade
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Introduces the club: Priya the precision-obsessed sophomore, Marcus who can't stop improvising, quiet Lupe who never tastes her own food. Dev watches Tamsin hold them together with duct-tape optimism. Beat: found-family warmth beginning to spark.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Gap
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Dev's POV alternating. Researching past champions for strategy, they discover 1979's pages razored out of every yearbook in the library. The librarian, Ms. Okonkwo, goes pale when asked and says some records were 'corrected.' Beat: first real crack in the school's polished story.

chapters.title: Cardamom in the Stairwell
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Detention in the east stairwell, he smells cardamom and finds a third note: a partial recipe, annotated in two different handwritings — one old, one unmistakably his father's. Beat: grief detonating quietly; the ghost knows his dad.

chapters.title: What Mom Won't Say
chapters.summary: Mom's POV, one rare waking hour. She notices Tamsin flinching at the word 'ghost,' remembers her husband's box of papers she's never opened. She almost tells Tamsin about the letter that arrived last spring, then doesn't. Beat: parental love tangled in protective silence.

chapters.title: Hargrove's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Snooping for budget money, Tamsin instead finds a locked drawer of 'archived' files — expulsion records, including one V., M., dated 1979. Hargrove catches him and issues a warning that sounds like a threat. Beat: the antagonist reveals the stakes are bigger than trophies.

chapters.title: Marisol Vane Taught Us to Read
chapters.summary: Ms. Okonkwo's POV. The librarian finally tells the story: Marisol Vane, a scholarship student expelled for running secret literacy-and-cooking classes for immigrant families in the home ec room, erased from every record at the district's orders. Beat: righteous anger; history as an act of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Recipe Is a Map
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cross-referencing the ghost's recipe fragments with his father's handwriting, Tamsin realizes the dish — a seven-step braided bread — encodes locations: the old home ec room, the sealed basement kitchen, the cornerstone. Beat: wonder; mystery becoming mission.

chapters.title: Regionals: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The regional semi-final collapses when the power cuts mid-bake; the team salvages disaster with a camp-stove improvisation and scrapes into finals. Tamsin leads brilliantly and then disappears before the photo. Beat: triumph undercut by Tamsin's retreat.

chapters.title: Nia Sees Her
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Ten-year-old Nia, waiting after school, sees a girl in a 1970s uniform in the east stairwell and isn't scared — she's charmed. She tells Tamsin the girl said, 'Tell your brother to stop reading alone.' Beat: wonder; the supernatural turning personal.

chapters.title: The Basement Kitchen
chapters.summary: Tamsin, Dev, Priya, and Lupe's shared POV sections. Following the recipe-map, they break into the sealed basement and find Marisol's preserved classroom: chalk lessons, forty names carved into a table, and a final page of the bread recipe guarded by a rusted lock. Beat: awe and trespass-guilt.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The ghost speaks at last — not words, but the ink itself forming sentences: Marisol's memory anchored to the school because her name was unmade. She needs to be remembered officially, or fade entirely. Tamsin realizes the final championship that matters is justice, not a trophy. Beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: Hargrove Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Hargrove's POV. Under pressure from the district to keep the Vane scandal buried before a centennial gala, Hargrove suspends the culinary club, confiscates their evidence, and threatens Tamsin's graduation clearance. Beat: cold institutional fear; the villain believes he's protecting the school.

chapters.title: The Letter Mom Kept
chapters.summary: Mom and Tamsin's alternating POV. Mom finally opens Dad's box: he was one of Marisol's students' children, and spent years petitioning the district to restore her record before he died. Mother and son grieve together, then plan. Beat: the family's silence breaking into partnership.

chapters.title: State Finals: The Braided Bread
chapters.summary: Lupe's POV. Reinstated after community outcry led by Ms. Okonkwo, the team bakes Marisol's completed recipe live at states — each braid a chapter of her story, narrated to the judges and crowd. They win, but the real victory is forty families in the audience recognizing their grandmother's teacher. Beat: catharsis; private grief made public feast.

chapters.title: The Centennial Gala
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the gala, Tamsin publicly presents the evidence, the carved table (donated by the families), and his father's letters. The board votes to restore Marisol Vane's record; Hargrove resigns rather than preside over it. Beat: justice achieved through truth-telling, not law.

chapters.title: Last Note, First Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the last day of school, the east stairwell smells of cardamom one final time. A note fades in — just 'Thank you, Tam' — then blank paper, warm to the touch. The weight lifts; the ghost is free. Beat: bittersweet release, gratitude without goodbye.

chapters.title: The Unofficial Recipe
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. Summer: Mom switched to day shifts, Nia runs a lemonade stand with Marisol's cookie recipe, and the culinary club — official now, plaque and all — teaches Saturday classes in the reopened home ec room. Tamsin writes his own recipe card for the wall: how to belong. Beat: earned peace; memory as inheritance.
